subject: Case study publish — sensitivity check after support incident
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Case study draft for Nimbus — need sensitivity check after June incident

Hi Soojin / Rishi,

Attaching the latest draft of the Nimbus Health case study (draft-nimbus-case-study-v2.docx). Legal and product signed off on story and metrics, but CS flagged the June 15th support incident (brief downtime for their integration) and asked we run a quick sensitivity review before we publish.

Key asks:
- Can one of you confirm whether we should pause publication or redact the incident reference?
- If we proceed, what phrasing is safe (site note vs. full paragraph)?
- I've attached the postmortem they provided (incident_postmortem_nimbus_20260615.pdf) and a quick redaction suggestions file.

Nimbus is a prioritized reference for Q3 PR — selling to health-tech customers; we don't want to damage trust but also don't want to lose timing if churn risk is low.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: draft-nimbus-case-study-v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), incident_postmortem_nimbus_20260615.pdf (application/pdf), redaction_suggestions.txt (text/plain)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Case study draft for Nimbus — need sensitivity check after June incident

Thanks for the context and the attachments, Marissa. Quick read: the draft mentions the incident in one paragraph under "operational lessons" and links to a short timeline.

My initial take: we should not lead with the incident. Options:
- Pause publish for 72 hours and request an explicit public statement from Nimbus that they are comfortable (preferred when customer is sensitive).
- Publish on schedule but replace the incident paragraph with a one-sentence note about "minor service disruption in June; full resolution & improvements were completed" and link to their public postmortem only if they approve.

Before deciding I want to loop in Rishi for risk and Hannah for CS perspective on churn. Rishi — can you confirm whether this qualifies as a release-blocking compliance issue? Hannah — did CS escalate to churn-risk?

Soojinn
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Marketing | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Case study draft for Nimbus — need sensitivity check after June incident

Soojinn / team — quick security/compliance read: the incident appears operational and confined to a single region for ~2 hours. The postmortem does not list any data exfiltration or PII exposure. From a compliance standpoint, nothing in the document triggers a regulatory disclosure requirement.

Recommendation: do not assert details beyond what Nimbus provides. If they volunteered a postmortem to us, prefer to host an excerpt only with their explicit signoff. I support "soft redaction" language in the draft if Nimbus expresses concern.

Will escalate to security if they share anything implying breach; as-is, not a blocker.

-Rishi
Director, Applied ML Security | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Case study draft for Nimbus — need sensitivity check after June incident

Marissa — CS sent a straightforward note: Nimbus is nervous about marketing copy right now because they had some inbound churn questions from two customers last month. They are not threatening to leave, but the CSM asks that we delay publishing until they finish a customer outreach campaign next week.

CS suggested either: pause publish until Aug 6 (after their outreach) or publish with extremely neutral phrasing and a link to their official statement (with their OK). They prefer a pause, but are OK with the neutral phrasing if we need the Q3 slot.

Given sales value and their request I lean pause for 9 days. Marissa — can you confirm whether Nimbus will accept a short embargo? If yes, we should send an approval email to Elena and ask for written signoff on the postmortem excerpt if we keep it.

-Hannah
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, NIMBUS-Sales <sales@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Request to embargo Redwood case study until Aug 6 — draft attached

Elena,

Thanks again for collaborating on the case study. We completed our internal review and want to respect Nimbus's timing. Per your team's recent note, we propose a brief embargo: Redwood will pause publishing the Nimbus case study until 2026-08-06. We'll also remove the detailed timeline paragraph and replace it with a neutral sentence referencing your public update, unless you confirm you'd like the postmortem excerpt included.

Please confirm the embargo and whether you want the brief neutral phrasing or the postmortem excerpt included. If you approve the excerpt, we'll need a short written signoff (email reply is fine).

If we don't hear back by Aug 3 we'll assume pause is fine and will queue the story for August 6.

Appreciate your partnership — we want to make sure the case study helps Nimbus with prospect conversations, not complicate them.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: draft-nimbus-case-study-v2.docx (updated for neutral phrasing), redaction_suggestions.txt
